# dsh-fastswitch
Makes **switching Sessions** in DeepSeek Harness fast. Two things, each independently switchable.
> 中文：README.zh.md
## What it fixes
When you switch a Session, DSH asks the Host for the opening history page. That page has a hard-code
d window — at least 50 messages — which on a long conversation arrives as a **2 MB** frame. That fra
me is the wait you feel.
Separately, while the page shells itself, several components each fetch the same read-only catalogs
on mount: `session/modelCatalog` 6 times, `credentials/describe` 7 times, `agentPresets/list` 6 time
s, `cotTranslation/limits` 3 times. No deduplication, no cache.
dsh-fastswitch makes one change for each, in the browser:
1. **Configurable opening window** — rewrites `turnWindow.minMessages` (50 → 20 by default) on the o
utgoing `session/follow` request. The Host validates `0 < minMessages <= maxMessages`, so this is a

supported request, not a patch. "Load earlier" pages (200 messages) are left untouched.
2. **Read-on
ly RPC dedupe + cache** — wraps `window.fetch`, caching read-only catalog calls for 5 minutes and co
llapsing concurrent ones into a single flight.
## Measured
Same machine, same page, same conversation:
| | default | with dsh-fastswitch |

| Opening snapshot (one long Session) | 2,040,432 B | **1,054,070 B** |
| `session/modelCatalog` | 6

calls | **1 call** |
| `credentials/describe` | 7 calls | **1 call** |
| `agentPresets/list` | 6 ca

lls | **1 call** |
| Total requests on first paint | 52 | **33** |
These come from a single measurement; they depend on conversation length and browser cache state, an
d are not constants.

## Configuration
All through `localStorage` — no config files:
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `dsh-fastswitch` | — | set to `off` to disable everything |
| `dsh-fastswitch-window` | `20` | ope

ning window size; `0` leaves it alone |
| `dsh-fastswitch-ttl` | `300000` | cache TTL in ms; `0` dis

ables caching |
| `dsh-fastswitch-merge` | `800` | concurrent-flight window in ms |
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Checking that it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `ws.rewritten` should increment once per Session switch;
- `fetch.hits + fetch.dedup` is the numbe
r of requests saved.
## Scope

- **Browser only.** Terminals, the SDK, ACP and other clients are unaffected.
- **Modifies no DeepSe
ek Harness file and no Host behaviour.** The window is a rewritten outgoing request; the cache is a

browser-side `fetch` wrapper. Uninstall and everything is back to stock.
- **No Session parking cach
e.** Keeping opened Sessions in memory for instant switch-back would mean operating on Session lifec

ycle internals, which breaks across versions. Deliberately out of scope.
- Caching covers **read-onl
y** catalogs only. No writes, no streaming responses, no auth endpoints.
## Compatibility

- Targets `dsh ^0.2.1-rc.2` (see `engines.dsh`).
- Both wrappers are idempotent, so HMR reloads do n

ot stack wrappers.
- If either wrapper cannot be installed it is skipped; the page degrades to stock
behaviour instead of breaking.
